text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained 0.44% today, capping a strong four-day rally that has recovered most of its losses from the prior week. The gain reflects a modest rebound in US crude prices (up to $89.62/barrel) and sustained refinery operations at 95.2% capacity, which keeps the company's processing margins intact even as global oil markets have shifted into oversupply—Russian production rebounded in October after a diesel deal, pushing worldwide supply above demand according to the International Energy Agency.

The broader headwind is that oil markets are returning to surplus, which typically pressures refiner margins, though the 59% spike in heating oil prices from last winter provides some offsetting lift for refined product demand as winter approaches. Marathon's stock is still down 6.76% over two weeks, suggesting investors are weighing the near-term tailwind of high heating oil prices against longer-term concerns about a softer global supply-demand balance.
